What counts—and what does not

140 categorized correctness cases

Only the named unit, functional, integration, and regression inventory contributes to 140. The separate transport-smoke gate owns its cross-process fixture assertions.

Separate release gates

Cross-process fixtures, module loaders, installed-package behavior, benchmark accounting, and tracked-record validation remain visible but never inflate correctness.

GatePurposeIn the 140?
Unit / functional / integration / regression140 named categorized behaviorsYes
Cross-process transport smoke · 8 assertionsStarts six legacy TCP, UDP4, UDP6, Unix, and Unix-sync fixtures; fails on crash, leak, forced termination, or nonzero exitNo
Runtime import / require smokeExercises main's native ESM entry through both supported loader pathsNo
Installed-package smokePacks, installs, and runs a real consumer outside the source treeNo
Benchmark harness · 11 checksValidates measurement isolation, exact accounting, cleanup, memory, and GC observationNo
Tracked benchmark validatorRejects malformed or ineligible benchmark records before publicationNo
CoverageExposes exercised and missed code pathsNo; evidence only

Run the gates

Complete project gate

npm test

Runs the 140 Vanilla Test cases with native V8 coverage, all three smoke gates, the 11 benchmark harness checks, and the tracked-record validator.

Benchmark evidence only

npm run benchmark:test
npm run benchmark:validate

Benchmark gates remain separate from correctness totals and measured vehicle comparisons.
